## GrepMesh search routing

<!-- grepmesh-routing:begin -->
For a known project or corpus, use XERJ for ranked code/documentation retrieval and external reference implementations; inspect its map and index freshness first. For an exact local path, identifier or literal, use bounded `rg`. Use GrepMesh only to discover an unknown host or project/root location across the fleet. Once the host and root are known, switch to XERJ or host-local `rg`; do not fan out through GrepMesh for ordinary searches in a known project. An empty or stale XERJ index is not evidence that source is absent: index the narrow authorized source folder or verify it with `rg`. XERJ is available through GPTAdmin as `mcp:shell:roomhacker-server-100:XERJ`; native clients also have the `xerj` MCP. External Hub search covers selected packs, not all GitHub. Preserve GrepMesh partial/host failure information.
<!-- grepmesh-routing:end -->

<!-- gptadmin-shared-workflow -->
## Shared engineering workflow (LHC + Agent Herder)

Applies to engineering and project work, including clients without local plugins.
Preserve the selected profile's domain/admin instructions and access restrictions.
This workflow grants no credentials, permissions or authority beyond the user's task.

- Use the existing project plan/board, keep source, review, merge, installation and live verification distinct. Record branch, exact commit, PR and evidence. Put large-task plans in the existing LHC plan, not a competing tracker.
- Each task uses its own branch and worktree from the verified integration target. Commit coherent changes (WIP included) and push the task branch freely: a branch is not a PR. Then deploy to the agreed or your own environment and manually exercise the real scenario. Open the PR ONLY after that scenario passed; it is the last step before integration. No early or draft PR for unfinished work; the plan link goes into the PR only then (check its audience/access first).
- Integrate through PRs, not direct writes to shared main. Follow the owner's existing merge/deploy policy and repository checks; do not invent extra approval questions for already authorized steps or bypass genuine permission/security gates. The owner's existing request for a result or deploy already authorizes deploying to their own service within that request: do not ask again. Respect the owner's explicit exclusions, system/harness limits and third-party service boundaries.
- Build candidates in an isolated staging area; do not move shared current/live pointers during build. Only the lease-admitted rollout changes live pointers. Use currently merged release scripts, not stale task-branch scripts that bypass guards.
- Before changing a shared runtime use Agent Herder project_release_lease status/acquire/renew/check with canonical project identity, session owner, token and fence. Re-read the live revision and enforce expected-revision CAS. Never overwrite a newer release with a stale artifact. Release in finally; terminal lifecycle events release ownership and TTL handles crashes. Ordinary turn completion is not session end. If Herder is unavailable for 3 minutes, do not wait: use the fallback git-ref lease refs/lhc/release/<project> (LHC 1.11.0) with the same CAS discipline.
- At terminal session end inventory project work and hand off unfinished integration. The last active worker owns whole-project integration, testing and cleanup. Use authoritative session state, not a guess from Git. Contact active owners through SendMessage.
- When bounded lookup finds no active owner of existing work, take responsibility: preserve exact commits and dirty diffs, record the adoption in the existing plan, inspect/review/test it and finish integration. Ambiguous ownership is not inactivity, and owner absence is not proof the changes are correct. Recheck ownership before mutation.
- Preserve active, dirty, conflicted, unmerged or unknown work. Clean up only verified merged, clean, inactive work under project coordination after rechecking HEAD and ownership. Never bulk-stash, reset foreign work, force-remove worktrees or blindly merge unknown branches.
- Reuse existing components and supported native install/release paths. Verify the exact installed revision and a harmless real consumer operation; tests, HTTP 200 or a receipt alone do not prove live acceptance. Keep unsupported clients, missing lifecycle evidence and remaining blockers explicit.
